sourceChecks.claim: AWS describes distribution across targets and adding/removing application capacity. The lesson explicitly scopes its illustrated round trip to a reverse proxy rather than every balancer architecture.
Azure distinguishes transport-level L4 and HTTP/path-aware L7, with TLS offload. The reused TCP connection consequence follows from the stated connection-level selection.
NGINX documents round robin, least active connections and weights, including unequal durations and capacity. The lesson correctly avoids treating counts or weights as a performance guarantee.
AWS documents periodic checks, thresholds and routing to unhealthy targets when all are unhealthy. This supports detection delay and the explicit fail-open caveat.
Microsoft explains web-farm shared state and the need for distributed cache/database storage; instance-local memory cannot supply another instance or survive loss merely because routing is sticky.
AWS documents stopping new requests during deregistration, waiting for in-flight work and connections, and errors when connections terminate early. The deadline interruption warning is consistent.
AWS requires stable operation identifiers and atomic token/mutation coordination; durable shared recognition supports a retry reaching another backend, unlike local memory.

Google SRE explains that balancing cannot prevent overload universally and advocates capacity-aware admission, degraded responses or errors. Surviving capacity and reachable entry are explicit whole-path design conditions.
